title: Recipe
description: A hearty and comforting vegan shepherd's pie, featuring a savory lentil and vegetable 'nest' baked under a golden, crystal-dusted sweet potato 'dune' topping. The perfect super-guard dish for a cold winter day.
name: Crystal-Topped Winter Lentil Nest

instructions.description: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the cubed sweet potatoes in a large pot, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Cook for 15-20 minutes or until fork-tender. Drain well.
While the potatoes are boiling, heat the olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the diced onion, carrots, and celery. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.

Add the minced garlic and chopped mushrooms to the pot. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, until the mushrooms have released their liquid and started to brown. Stir in the tomato paste, smoked paprika, thyme, and cumin, and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Stir in the rinsed lentils, diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, and tamari. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer. Cover and cook for 25-30 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the mixture has thickened. Stir in the frozen peas and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Mash the cooked sweet potatoes with the plant-based milk, melted vegan butter, a pinch of nutmeg, salt, and pepper until smooth and creamy.
Spread the lentil 'nest' mixture evenly into a 9x13 inch baking dish or a similar-sized casserole dish.
Carefully spoon the mashed sweet potato over the lentil base and spread evenly to 'guard' the filling. Use the back of a fork to create a 'dune'-like texture on top.
Sprinkle the top with the coarse 'crystal' sea salt and an extra dusting of smoked paprika.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the filling is bubbly and the topping is lightly golden. Let it rest for 10 minutes before serving.

notes: For a richer flavor, add a splash of vegan red wine to the lentil mixture after sautéing the vegetables. You can substitute sweet potatoes with regular russet or Yukon Gold potatoes for a more traditional shepherd's pie topping.
